definitions.gloss: doyō; 18-day period before each season change
definitions.explanation: In the traditional Japanese calendar, the ~18 days leading up to each new season (spring, summer, autumn, winter). The summer {土用|どよう} is the best known, associated with eating eel.

examples.english: We eat eel on the Day of the Ox during doyō.

examples.japanese: {土用|どよう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}る→入る：00494_hairu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{暑|あつ}さ→暑さ：12973_atsusa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{本格的|ほんかくてき}→本格的：05681_honkakuteki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: Once doyō starts, the heat sets in for real.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{土用|どよう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{期間中|きかんちゅう}→期間中：23950_kikanchuu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{土|つち}→土：02229_tsuchi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{動|うご}かして→動かす：01885_ugokasu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧いけない⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われていた→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: In the old days, it was said that you should not disturb the earth during doyō.

notes:
Originates from the traditional five-element calendar. Strictly, there are four {土用|どよう} periods each year, but in modern usage 'doyō' almost always means the summer one in late July to early August.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {土用|どよう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{丑|うし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧: 'Day of the Ox' during doyō — the day to eat eel
- {土用|どよう}{入|い}り: the start of a doyō period
- {土用|どよう}{波|なみ}: rough late-summer waves
- ⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{土用|どよう}: summer doyō

CULTURAL NOTE:
The summer {土用|どよう} falls in the hottest part of the year. There is a tradition of eating eel (うなぎ) on the {丑|うし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧ (Day of the Ox) within this period to build stamina against the heat — a custom popularized in the Edo period and still observed today.
